model_conventions.checked_scope: AppendixD2DensitySource.lean derives a.e. density zero above M from the literal PDF law, the reflected tail-mass integral identity by interval substitution, local integrability, the CDF-power sandwich, and then the D.2, Lemma 1, and Theorem 1(ii) endpoints. No tail, split, or optimizer certificate is accepted from callers. It does not claim a translated/lower-tail extension outside the recorded nonnegative convention.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: The phrase 'D has pdf f_D' is represented by a probability measure equal to Lebesgue volume with density ofReal(f_D), with f_D nonnegative, measurable, and integrable. The Theorem 1(ii) allocation endpoint additionally adopts an a.e. nonnegative conditional-value convention. Given that convention, its lower endpoint L, positive width, and positive M are support normalizations rather than separate claims about every merely upper-bounded translated law.
model_conventions.why_needed: The source proof silently changes from a reflected density to an integral representation of upper-tail mass and then to CDF-power bounds. These are not theorem-name consequences of a function called pdf: they require an actual density measure and enough boundedness/integrability for the expected top-k loss to be well defined. The source says only bounded above, so the nonnegative value-domain convention must remain visible rather than being inferred from the tail formula.

model_conventions.checked_scope: PaperInterface.theorem1_ii_formulaSpec, theorem1_iii_formulaSpec, theorem1_iv_formulaSpec, and corollary1Spec visibly retain strict positivity of each preferred-type mass and existentially select the source's finite optima. Corollary 1 also returns an explicit probability law D, tied to the concrete iid model branch. Their PMF-selected source objectives and fixed-k conclusions are checked only on that regular all-coordinate domain. The stronger universal formulas remain support and the convention does not assert a zero-support extension.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: For the checked fixed-k gamma-share endpoints that assert a limiting representation for every named type, the source-selected preferred-type PMF has strictly positive mass at every type. This is an additional regularity condition on the all-coordinate route, not a claim that the archival model text excluded zero-probability types.
model_conventions.why_needed: The source says only that one type is selected with probabilities p_t, which permits zero masses. The direct all-coordinate optimizer-share arguments use positive weights and finite normalized powers for every coordinate; a zero-probability type instead requires a separate supportwise formulation and optimizer-selection analysis. Recording the restriction prevents that zero-support boundary from being smuggled into a source theorem match.

model_conventions.checked_scope: Theorem2RankBernoulliSource.lean uses EconCSLib.pmfPi, proves the atom formula and both expectations, and the corrected PaperInterface endpoints include those equalities in their conclusions. Top-one adds c>0 and q_1<1 for arbitrary-optimum homogeneity; positive-alpha all-consumed needs q_1<=1; alpha zero uses the recorded selected-optimizer convention.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: For each type and finite count, the rank coordinates are independent Boolean variables with rank-specific success parameter c*((i+1)+d)^(-alpha). They are not asserted iid across ranks; cross-type independence is neither asserted nor needed because one preferred type is evaluated.
model_conventions.why_needed: The product top-one objective requires within-type independence, while the all-consumed sum objective only needs the rankwise means. The source uses inconsistent iid wording, so the actual finite PMF and its expectation identities must be checked before asymptotic objective theorems receive source-model credit.

model_conventions.checked_scope: AllConsumedIidSource.lean derives the common-mean linear objective from a finite iid sample law. PaperInterface.theorem1_v_source_experiment_formula and PaperInterface.theorem1_v_selected_maximizer_conclusion separately expose the PMF experiment, integrability, nonnegative mean, and selected all-on likelihood-maximizing optimum. Strict uniqueness remains a separate strengthening, not a claim about every tied optimum.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: For the all-consumed common-distribution endpoint, the common conditional mean is nonnegative for the weak argmax direction and positive for the unique argmax direction.
model_conventions.why_needed: When every item is consumed, the objective is linear in the common mean. A negative common mean reverses the stated argmax direction, and a zero mean eliminates uniqueness.
